originality.rationale: Primary full-text and published result comparisons found no implication of the ordinary Heawood five-cut wedge of 491 eight-spheres. The closest uniform theorem assumes girth at least seven for five-cuts; Heawood has girth six, with an explicit 28-hexagon discrepancy. Searches cannot rule out every unindexed equivalent result. The number 28 of Heawood hexagons is already published; novelty concerns the cut-complex homotopy type and topological correction, not the hexagon count.
residual_risks: A logically equivalent five-cut result might exist in unindexed or inaccessible literature.

value.rationale: The Heawood graph is the canonical cubic girth-six Fano incidence graph. Five-cuts are the first natural parameter for this graph not covered by the published girth-based k=4 theorem; the 28 induced six-cycles cause exactly 28 missing next-to-top faces and a 28-sphere correction. A complete integral homotopy classification with explanatory combinatorics and a reproducible certificate is a motivated boundary case rather than an arbitrary numerical slice.
